title: Subjunctive and formal structures
grammar: Subjunctive, It is essential that, I would rather

sections.heading: What is the subjunctive?
sections.body: The subjunctive is a verb form used in formal English to express demands, recommendations, wishes or hypothetical situations. It is very common in formal writing and after certain expressions.

sections.heading: Present subjunctive
sections.body: After certain verbs and expressions, we use the base form of the verb (no -s, no 'to') for all subjects.
table: It is essential that + subject + base verb
It is essential that he be informed.
I suggest that + subject + base verb
I suggest that she stay at home.
I recommend that + subject + base verb
I recommend that you take a break.
I insist that + subject + base verb
I insist that he come with us.

sections.heading: Common triggers
list: It is important / essential / vital / crucial that...
It is necessary that...
I suggest / recommend / propose that...
I insist / demand / request that...
The doctor advised that...
The rules require that...

sections.heading: Would rather / Would sooner
sections.body: Used to express preferences about the present or past.
table: I would rather you didn't smoke here.
I would rather you had told me.

sections.heading: It's time + past simple
sections.body: Expresses that something should have happened already.
list: It's time we left.
It's time you went to bed.
It's high time we did something about this.

sections.heading: Formal 'if' clauses with inversion
list: Were I you, I would apologise. (instead of 'If I were you')
Had I known, I would have called. (instead of 'If I had known')
Should you need anything, please ask. (instead of 'If you should need')

sections.heading: Common mistakes
list: Do not add -s to the subjunctive: 'It is essential that he goes' → 'It is essential that he go' (formal).
Do not use 'would' after 'if' in hypothetical clauses.
Remember: after 'would rather' with a different subject, use the past simple.

list.definition: It is essential that everyone be present.
It is vital that we act now.
It is crucial that the report be finished today.
It is necessary that you sign here.
I recommend that you take a day off.
I insist that he come with us.
I suggest that we leave early.
I propose that we change the plan.
The manager requested that we be quiet.
I urge that we take action now.
I would sooner you didn't tell anyone.
It's time we made a decision.
It's high time you found a job.
Were I you, I would decline.
Had I known, I would have acted differently.
Should you need help, contact us.

phases.name: Discovery
phases.intro: Look at these sentences. Read them carefully and think about the questions below.
sentences: It is essential that he be informed immediately.
I suggest that she stay at home tonight.
I would rather you didn't smoke here.
Were I you, I would apologise.
Had I known, I would have called.
The doctor advised that he rest for a week.
They demanded that the meeting be postponed.
questions: In sentences 1, 2, 7 and 8, what form of the verb is used after 'that'?
In sentence 3, why is the past simple used after 'would rather'?
In sentence 4, what does 'it's time + past simple' express?
In sentences 5 and 6, what replaces 'if' in these formal structures?
Why is the subjunctive considered formal?

questions.prompt: It is important that she ___ on time.
questions.explanation: Subjunctive uses the base form: be, not is.

questions.prompt: I would rather you ___ tell anyone.
questions.explanation: I would rather + past simple for present/future wishes.

questions.prompt: I suggest that he ___ a doctor.
___ I you, I would accept the offer.
It's time we ___ this problem.
The manager demanded that the report ___ by Friday.
___ I known, I would have told you.
I recommend that everyone ___ the instructions.
It's high time you ___ a decision.
___ you need help, please contact me.

phases.name: Free practice
prompts: Write 5 formal recommendations using 'It is essential/important that...'.
Write 5 sentences with 'I would rather' + past simple about situations you would like to change.
Rewrite 5 conditional sentences using formal inversion (Were I..., Had I..., Should you...).

I'd rather you ___ come tomorrow.

questions.explanation: Past regret: would rather + past perfect.

sections.heading: Key rules
list: Subjunctive: base form after 'It is essential that...', 'I suggest that...', etc.
Common triggers: essential, important, vital, crucial, necessary, suggest, recommend, insist, demand.
I would rather + subject + past simple (present) / past perfect (past).
It's time / It's high time + past simple.
Formal inversion: Were I..., Had I..., Should you...

sections.heading: Common mistakes
list: Do not add -s to the subjunctive in formal contexts.
Do not use 'would' after 'if' in hypothetical clauses.
Remember: 'would rather' + different subject uses past simple.

sections.heading: Useful phrases
list: It is essential that...
I recommend that...
I would rather you...
It's time we...
Were I you...
Had I known...
Should you need...
